subject: Clarifying pen-test scope for FinBank VPC & remediation update
messages:
From: Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@finbank.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinc.com>
Cc: security@finbank.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test artifacts and VPC boundary questions for Private deploy

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are progressing our internal procurement checklist and need a few clarifications before legal signs off on the Private deployment. Specifically: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwood's most recent penetration test (July 2026) included testing against customer-managed network boundaries when the customer runs Redwood in a VPC (i.e. private deployment)?
- If not, do you have any customer-specific guidance or evidence you share by request (network diagrams, attack surface assumptions, list of external-facing endpoints hosted in the customer VPC)?
- For findings relevant to our environment, can you share remediation status and whether you plan a targeted retest inside the customer VPC or if you advise customers to run their own engagement?

We need redacted artifacts to attach to our SIG questionnaire: a one-page scope summary, the high-level list of findings (no PII), and a diagram showing the boundary assumptions. A timeline for retest/remediation would also be helpful.

Appreciate a response by EOD Wednesday so we can keep our review on track.

Best,
Alice Sullivan
Security Manager, FinBank
From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinc.com>
To: Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@finbank.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwoodinc.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinc.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinc.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test artifacts and VPC boundary questions for Private deploy

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise answer and attached are the redacted artifacts you requested.

Short answers:
- Our July 2026 internal penetration test covered Redwood-hosted and Redwood-managed enclaves (hosted/dedicated). It did not include explicit blackbox testing inside customer-managed VPCs because those are customer isolated networks with different network policies and IP addressing.
- We provide a boundary assumptions diagram and a one-page scope summary that maps our responsibilities vs. the customer’s (attached: vpc-boundary-diagram-finbank-params.png, redwood-pen-test-summary-2026-07-redacted.pdf).
- For high-risk findings that could be affected by customer network configuration (e.g., exposed management interfaces, misrouted subnets), we track remediation in a shared sheet and recommend a scoped customer-specific retest. We can arrange a targeted retest (Redwood-run) inside the customer's VPC under an engagement statement, or we can provide the findings and recommended test cases for your vendor to run.

Attachments (redacted):
- redwood-pen-test-summary-2026-07-redacted.pdf — executive-scope + high-level findings (no exploitation logs)
- vpc-boundary-diagram-finbank-params.png — shows expected SGs, NAT/IGW placement, and where Redwood-managed endpoints terminate
- remediation-tracking-sheet-2026-08.csv — remediation status for items tagged as VPC-relevant

Next steps I propose:
1) We (Redwood) review the remediation sheet with your security team and flag items that need retest inside your VPC.
2) If you want Redwood to run the retest, we’ll draft a narrow scoping addendum (dates, IP ranges, allowed tooling, PoC rules).
3) If you prefer your vendor, we’ll provide a test-case list and an environment checklist.

I’ll loop Dev for the technical boundary explanation and a recommended retest plan. Please let me know preferred times for a 30-minute sync tomorrow or Wednesday.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwoodinc.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinc.com>, Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@finbank.com>

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test artifacts and VPC boundary questions for Private deploy

Thanks Rachel — adding technical detail for Alice and FinBank.

Context and boundary assumptions (short):
- Redwood Private runs a control plane outside the customer VPC by default; customer hosts inference workers (containers/VMs) inside their VPC that talk to the control plane over TLS. In some on-prem configurations the control plane is also customer-hosted — we document both options.
- The July 2026 pen test validated Redwood-managed control plane components and the default worker image used by Redwood-managed deployments. It did not perform lateral-movement testing inside a customer VPC because we do not have access to customer-managed subnets or security groups.

Important implications for FinBank:
- If your VPC exposes any management endpoints (SSH, K8s API) to public IP ranges or to cross-account roles, those are in-scope for your vendor/retainer; Redwood’s test results assume those endpoints are protected by your network controls.
- Findings in our report that reference "service misconfiguration" or "exposed admin console" assume the default deployment topology in the boundary diagram. Where FinBank customizes network ACLs or NAT behavior the exploitability and remediation steps may differ.

Recommended retest approach for customer VPCs (options):
A) Redwood-Run Scoped Retest — Redwood security team runs an in-scope engagement inside your VPC with a one-week window. Scope: IP ranges, target host list, limited toolset (no noisy automated mass-scanning), and agreed PoC rules. Good when FinBank wants vendor continuity.
B) Customer-Run Verification — We provide test cases, artifacts, and a remediation checklist so your vendor performs the retest. Redwood will validate results and sign off on remediation. Faster procurement but requires your vendor time.

We flagged three findings in the attached remediation sheet as "VPC-impact": IDs R-23, R-45, R-77. Current status: R-23 mitigated (config change, verified), R-45 in progress (expected 2026-08-20), R-77 accepted risk by product (requires cross-team rollout; ETA 2026-09-03).

If FinBank prefers the Redwood-Run option, we will need a signed scoping addendum and temporary test credentials (jump host or temporary IAM role) with IP allow-listing.

- Dev Patel
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

- If Redwood-Run is chosen: Targeted retest window 2026-08-23 to 2026-08-27 (one-week window).

Action items for FinBank:

Thanks —
Rachel
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
